questions.stem: In the expression P(B | A), the vertical bar is read as the word…
options: divided, so the bar means a ratio
and, so both events must happen together
given, so A is already known true
or, so either one event may happen
questions.correctFeedback: The bar means "given". P(B|A) is the chance of B once you already know A happened.
questions.incorrectFeedback: It reads as "given". A division does appear in the formula, but the bar itself is not the division sign.

questions.stem: From Lesson 1: two fair dice are rolled. The chance that at least one shows a six is…
options: eleven over thirty-six, by the complement
two over six, one per die
one over thirty-six, both showing six
ten over thirty-six, minus both sixes
questions.correctFeedback: Right — no six on either die is 5 × 5 = 25 of 36 pairs, so at least one six is 1 − 25/36 = 11/36.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Use the complement: no six anywhere is 25 of the 36 pairs, so 1 − 25/36 = 11/36. Adding 1/6 + 1/6 counts the pair 6-6 twice.

questions.stem: A bag holds 5 white and 3 green balls. Two are drawn without replacement. P(both white) is…
options: five over eight times five over eight
five over eight plus four over seven
five over eight times three over eight
five over eight times four over seven
questions.correctFeedback: Right — (5/8) × (4/7) = 20/56 = 5/14. The second factor is conditional: one white is already gone.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Use P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B|A). First draw 5/8; then 7 balls remain with 4 white, so (5/8) × (4/7) = 5/14.

questions.stem: Two events A and B each have probability above zero and cannot both occur. They are…
options: independent, since one rules out other
not independent, since one rules other
independent only if P(A) equals P(B)
independent whenever P(A) exceeds one half
questions.correctFeedback: Correct. Mutually exclusive means P(A ∩ B) = 0, but independence needs P(A)P(B), which is above zero. So they cannot be independent.
questions.incorrectFeedback: They are NOT independent. Learning A occurred tells you B certainly did not — that is maximal information, the opposite of independence.
